\sum_{v\in V(D)}|N^{+2}(v)|\geq \sum_{v\in V(D)}|N^{+}(v)|.
$$

Equivalently, the average size of the second out-neighborhood is at least the average size of the first out-neighborhood. The supplied source attributes this conjecture to Conjecture 6.15 of Sullivan and gives no evidence that it has been resolved.

343632.title: The Hepp-bound faithfulness conjecture for primitive phi-four graphs
343632.review_depth: Panzer Conjecture 1.2 and period/Hepp definitions, plus Schnetz five-twist arXiv:2505.02578 Section 4 discussion inspected.
343632.literal_statement: Let $G$ be a graph that is p-logarithmic in $d=4$ dimensions and whose vertices all have degree at most $4$; call such a graph a $\phi^4$ graph. Let $\mathcal{P}(G)$ denote its period and $\mathcal{H}(G)$ its Hepp bound. **Hepp-bound faithfulness conjecture.** Two $\phi^4$ graphs have equal periods if and only if they have equal Hepp bounds. The conjecture is supported by computations for primitive $\phi^4$ graphs through $11$ loops, but remains open; it is motivated by analogous conjectures for the $c_2$ invariant and the permanent.
343632.mathematical_attempt_or_disposition: Five-twist paper retains the Hepp faithfulness conjecture and discusses new period identities, many involving non-phi4 graphs. Those do not by themselves refute the reserved primitive phi4 assertion.
343632.precise_remaining_gap: Need phi4 pair with certified unequal Hepp bounds and exact equal periods, or equal Hepp bounds and rigorously unequal periods. Numerical integration differences cannot certify it. No graph-invariant sweep run because no rigorous period-separation checker established.
